books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the account of party realignment in Barron’s Premium 2027, Chapter 7, Topic 5.6, and 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 14. The facts are as stated in the books; the wording is original.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase: The Kansas-Nebraska Act split the Whig Party between its proslavery “Cotton Whigs” and its antislavery “Conscience Whigs,” and the party fell apart in the elections of 1854. Former Whigs, Free-Soilers, antislavery Democrats, and abolitionists joined in 1854 to form the Republican Party, built on the free-labor idea that a worker could rise by his own labor. The new party opposed letting slavery spread into the territories, though it did not call for abolishing slavery where it already existed.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The collapse of the Whigs described in the passage most directly shows that by 1854

options.text: the Democrats had become a party of the North.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the Democrats became stronger in the South and more explicitly proslavery, not a Northern party.

options.text: slavery had broken the old parties along sectional lines.
the Know-Nothings had taken control of the South.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the Know-Nothings split over slavery and faded; they never took over the South.

options.text: the new Republicans had already won the presidency.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the Republicans would not win the presidency until 1860; Frémont lost in 1856.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the Democrats became stronger in the South and more explicitly proslavery, not a Northern party.
rationales.B: The Whigs split into Cotton and Conscience wings and collapsed, while the Democrats turned Southern and proslavery.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the Know-Nothings split over slavery and faded; they never took over the South.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the Republicans would not win the presidency until 1860; Frémont lost in 1856.
rationales.general:
1. Watch the Whigs: Cotton Whigs against Conscience Whigs, split over slavery.
2. Watch the result: the party fell apart in the elections of 1854.
3. Watch the Democrats: they survived by turning Southern and proslavery.
4. See the outcome: the Whigs vanished from the presidential race by 1856, replaced by the Republicans.
Remember: when one question splits every party the same way, the parties will be rebuilt around that question.
